title: Subtraction of 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Subtraction – Primary 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Subtract 2-digit numbers with and without exchanging; know subtraction facts to 20; check subtraction by addition. (summary of the NERDC Primary 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 maths worksheets on subtraction: facts to 20, fact families, subtracting tens, subtracting 2-digit numbers and checking with addition. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Take away the units, then the tens
key_sub: Check: answer + number taken = first number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Take away the units first, then the tens.
  • If there are not enough units, exchange 1 ten for 10 units.
  • Check your answer by adding.

Examples

Example

43 − 18

Exchange: 13 − 8 = 5

3 − 1 = 2

Answer: 25

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking the small digit from the big oneIn 43 − 18 do 13 − 8, not 8 − 3.
Forgetting to exchangeCross out the ten and write one less.
Subtracting in the wrong orderThe bigger number comes first.

faq.a: Add the answer and the number you took away.

items.e: Think addition: 8 + 5 = 13. So 13 − 8 = 5.
Think addition: 9 + 6 = 15. So 15 − 9 = 6.
Think addition: 7 + 5 = 12. So 12 − 7 = 5.
Think addition: 8 + 8 = 16. So 16 − 8 = 8.
Think addition: 6 + 8 = 14. So 14 − 6 = 8.
Start at 12 and count back 3: 11, 10, 9. Do not count 12 itself. 12 − 3 = 9.
Start at 11 and count back 2: 10, 9. Do not count 11 itself. 11 − 2 = 9.
Start at 15 and count back 3: 14, 13, 12. Do not count 15 itself. 15 − 3 = 12.
Start at 17 and count back 2: 16, 15. Do not count 17 itself. 17 − 2 = 15.
16 − 6 = 10. You must take away 9 in all, and 6 is done. So take away 3 more: 10 − 3 = 7.
13 − 3 = 10. You must take away 5 in all, and 3 is done. So take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.
11 − 1 = 10. You must take away 4 in all, and 1 is done. So take away 3 more: 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 6 + 9 = 15?
items.e: The family of 6, 9 and 15: 6 + 9 = 15, 9 + 6 = 15, 15 − 6 = 9, 15 − 9 = 6. Only 15 − 9 = 6 uses all three numbers.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 7 + 5 = 12?
items.e: The family of 7, 5 and 12: 7 + 5 = 12, 5 + 7 = 12, 12 − 7 = 5, 12 − 5 = 7. Only 12 − 7 = 5 uses all three numbers.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 8 + 9 = 17?
items.e: The family of 8, 9 and 17: 8 + 9 = 17, 9 + 8 = 17, 17 − 8 = 9, 17 − 9 = 8. Only 9 + 8 = 17 uses all three numbers.
Count up from 9 to 10, then to 15: 9 + 1 = 10, 10 + 5 = 15. 1 + 5 = 6, so the missing number is 6.
Count up from 7 to 10, then to 13: 7 + 3 = 10, 10 + 3 = 13. 3 + 3 = 6, so the missing number is 6.
Count up from 8 to 10, then to 12: 8 + 2 = 10, 10 + 2 = 12. 2 + 2 = 4, so the missing number is 4.
Count up from 6 to 10, then to 14: 6 + 4 = 10, 10 + 4 = 14. 4 + 4 = 8, so the missing number is 8.
Think addition: 7 + 8 = 15. Check: 15 − 7 = 8. 1 is wrong because 8 − 7 = 1 goes the other way.

items.q: The frames show 8 + 5 = 13. What is 13 − 5?
items.e: Take away the 5 blue counters. The 8 red counters are left. 13 − 5 = 8.
If 8 + 5 = 13, then 13 − 8 = 5. Subtraction undoes addition.

items.q: Which subtraction matches the model?
items.e: Start with the whole and take away one part. The other part is left: 13 − 8 = 5.

items.q: Which addition matches the model?
items.e: Add the two parts to get the whole: 12 + 8 = 20.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 7 + 4 = 11?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers: 7, 4 and 11. 11 − 4 = 7 uses them all.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family for 6, 9 and 15?
items.e: 9 − 6 = 3 uses the number 3, not 15. The others use only 6, 9 and 15.

items.q: How many facts are in the fact family for 5, 8 and 13?

items.e: Think: 5 + 8 = 13. So 13 − 5 = 8. (12 comes from 5 − 3 in the units.)
Think: 6 + 8 = 14. So 14 − 6 = 8. (12 comes from 6 − 4 in the units.)
Think: 6 + 14 = 20. So 20 − 6 = 14. (4 is the bond to 10, not to 20.)
Think: 3 + 8 = 11. So 11 − 3 = 8. (12 comes from 3 − 1 in the units.)
Add the answer to the number you took away. 8 + 8 = 16, so 16 − 8 = 8 is right.

items.e: The whole is the two parts added: 6 + 9 = 15. (3 is 9 − 6.)

items.e: Whole − part = the other part. 17 − 9 = 8. Check: 9 + 8 = 17.

items.q: These blocks show 52. You want to take away 27. There are only 2 units, so you cannot take away 7 units. What should you do first?
items.e: Trade 1 ten for 10 units. Now there are 4 tens and 12 units. Take away 7 units: 12 − 7 = 5. Take away 2 tens: 4 − 2 = 2. 52 − 27 = 25.
Units: 3 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 36. Check: 36 + 27 = 63.

items.q: Add the tens, then the units. What is 35 + 42?
items.e: Add the tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Add the units: 5 + 2 = 7. Then 70 + 7 = 77.

items.q: Take away the tens, then the units. What is 63 − 28?
items.e: Take away the tens first: 63 − 20 = 43. Then take away 8. Go back to the ten: 43 − 3 = 40, then 40 − 5 = 35.

items.q: Use the blocks. What is 47 + 38?
items.e: Tens: 4 + 3 = 7 tens. Units: 7 + 8 = 15 units. Exchange 10 units for 1 ten: 8 tens and 5 units. 47 + 38 = 85.

items.q: 1 ten was exchanged for 10 units, so 54 is 4 tens and 14 units. 26 is crossed out. What is 54 − 26?
items.e: 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens. 14 units − 6 units = 8 units. 2 tens and 8 units make 28. 54 − 26 = 28.

items.q: Add 20, then take away 1. What is 46 + 19?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. 46 + 20 = 66. Then 66 − 1 = 65. (66 forgets to take away 1.)
Subtraction undoes addition. Start at 85 and take away 38: 85 − 38 = 47.

You can add in any order. 9 + 6 is the same as 6 + 9, so the answer is 15.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 7 + 8?
items.e: Addition can be done in any order. 8 + 7 = 15, and 7 + 8 = 15.
Swapping the numbers in an addition gives the same answer: 6 + 9 = 9 + 6. You cannot swap the numbers in a subtraction.
No. 12 − 5 means take 5 from 12. 5 − 12 means take 12 from 5. Order matters in subtraction.

items.q: You can swap the numbers in one of these and get the same answer. Which one?
items.e: Only addition can be done in any order. 4 + 11 = 11 + 4 = 15. So the answer is 4 + 11.

items.q: Joy says 10 − 3 is the same as 3 − 10. Is she right?
items.e: 10 − 3 = 7, but you cannot take 10 from 3 and get 7. Order matters in subtraction.

items.e: The parts are 8 and 6. You can add them in any order: 8 + 6 = 14 and 6 + 8 = 14.

items.q: Amaka says 13 − 4 = 8. Check with addition. Is she right?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 8 + 4 = 12, not 13. So she is not right. 13 − 4 = 9.

items.q: Ikenna says 100 − 60 = 40. Which addition checks it?
items.e: Add the answer to the number taken away: 40 + 60 = 100. So Ikenna is right.
